- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.20) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices after strong negative sentiment spikes — adjust downward bias by 2–5% of recent range.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves — cap forecast at 1.5x recent high or 10% below next-day true value.
- Mean-revert forecasts when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative (sentiment < -0.20) — apply 0.5–1.0% downward correction.
- Lagged forecasts overreact to recent sentiment — delay peak predictions by 1–2 days if sentiment is trending.
- Avoid overconfidence in short-term spikes — reduce forecast volatility if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, reduce forecast mean by 1–3% and shift downward by 1–2 days.
- Correct for “sentiment lag” — if sentiment peaks 2+ days before price peak, forecast should be adjusted to align with sentiment timing.
